correctness.rationale: Every connected partition of a star has exactly one hub-containing bundle; all other nonempty shares are singleton leaves. For a selected center-leaf set, ordinary EF1 is equivalent to the minimum outside leaf value being at least the hub-bundle value after removing its largest item. Swapping an included larger leaf for an excluded smaller one weakly lowers that trimmed value and weakly raises the minimum outside value, proving the exact general prefix criterion. A dominant hub and strictly positive distinct leaf values force the unique prefix hub bundle, yielding 0 or \(n!\) labeled assignments. Starting leaf weights 2,3 and setting the next weight to the preceding prefix sum or preceding weight plus 1 yields the exact prescribed feasibility bit and strict integer increase. The five-vertex example and smallest-star claim follow by the n=3 c=k-2 boundary. The standalone verifier directly checks 320 agent-count comparisons, 510 prescribed feasibility words, 3586 constructed agent-count positions, and the labeled five-vertex counts.

originality.rationale: The inspected papers address universal connected-EF1 or outer-EF1 guarantees across valuation profiles, or different nonmonotone cut-valuations and efficiency requirements. They do not imply a fixed common strictly positive valuation realizing arbitrary binary agent-count feasibility patterns, nor the 0-or-\(n!\) exact labeled allocation census. Own accessible mathematical claims concern friendship graphs under binary valuations and general biclique universal spectra, not this weighted-star fixed-profile theorem. This assessment is best-knowledge rather than a proof that no unpublished equivalent exists.

value.rationale: The agent-count feasibility spectrum is motivated directly by the core question of the initiating connected fair-division paper. Exact profile-wise realizability is surprising because the graph, goods and positive additive common valuation stay fixed as n changes, yet there is no forbidden interior binary pattern. The proof also gives a constructive decision criterion and an exact full labeled allocation census (0 or \(n!\) under dominant hub), and identifies a sharp five-vertex 2-yes/3-no/4-yes example. This is a structural expressiveness theorem rather than a selected small experiment or a numerical table.
